pilot: generic-methodology workflow family (diagnose-failure, document-architecture, explore-directions, threat-model, polish-issue)
purpose: Decide whether these workflow skills earn their keep. Each produces an artifact (a diagnosis, an architecture doc, strategic directions, a threat model, a polished issue) from a self-contained scenario. The A/B measures whether the skill's methodology prose makes the artifact better than a capable bare model produces from the same scenario. Caveat for interpretation: document-architecture and explore-directions also encode a file/format CONVENTION (docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/directions/) which is a KEEP-worthy objective even if content quality ties — the anchors judge substantive methodology; a tie means 'the only residual value is the convention', decided separately.

arms.A_control: Reads the skill's registry/<skill>/SKILL.md methodology and applies it to the scenario.
arms.B_bare: Capable bare model, same scenario, no skill.

protocol: Blind answer + blind deterministic-anchor scoring (evals/family_ab.workflow.js). gate in evals/README.md.

gate.evict_if: mean(B) >= mean(A) - 0.10 AND no B-only must_exclude violation where A has none
gate.note: A skill whose content-quality ties but which enforces a durable file/format convention is a KEEP-as-convention, not a blanket evict.

must_include: forms more than one candidate hypothesis for the flakiness (e.g. timing/async race, shared state/order dependence, external dependency, resource/timeout) rather than guessing one cause

proposes a discriminating experiment or evidence to gather that would confirm/refute a hypothesis (e.g. run in isolation, seed/order variation, add timing/logging), i.e. an evidence loop, not a blind fix
must_exclude: jumps straight to a code fix without establishing the root cause
attributes it to one cause with no evidence or alternative considered

must_include: distinguishes root cause from symptom and reasons from the available evidence (logs/timing/correlation) toward the most likely cause
names the next concrete diagnostic step (a focused experiment, log, or metric) that would narrow it, staying read-only rather than shipping a speculative fix
must_exclude: immediately proposes a patch as the answer without diagnosis
conflates the surface error with its underlying cause

must_include: produces the core architecture views for the described system: at least a system-context view, a runtime/request-flow view, and module/service boundaries
grounds the description in the system's actual named components and their responsibilities rather than generic boilerplate, and is honest about what is derived vs assumed
must_exclude: invents components or flows not implied by the described system
produces a single vague prose blob with no structural decomposition or diagram

must_include: traces the data/request path through the named components end to end (entry -> processing -> storage/egress), identifying the trust and module boundaries it crosses
captures the data model / key entities and where state lives, distinguishing derived-from-description facts from assumptions
must_exclude: describes an idealized generic architecture instead of the one described
omits where data is stored or how it flows

must_include: generates at least 3 genuinely distinct strategic directions (different bets/audiences/mechanisms), not incremental variations of one idea
gives each direction evidence/rationale grounded in the described state AND its trade-offs or risks, so they can be compared
must_exclude: offers a single recommendation or a to-do list rather than distinct strategic options
lists directions with no trade-offs, evidence, or basis for choosing

must_include: diagnoses the gap between where the product is and where it could go before proposing directions
presents 3-5 distinct directions each with a rationale and an explicit trade-off, framed as options for the user to choose, not a single plan
must_exclude: jumps to one growth tactic without exploring the option space
proposes directions that are minor variants of the same approach

must_include: systematically enumerates assets, actors/entry points, and trust boundaries the feature crosses (not just a list of generic vulns)
derives concrete abuse cases and maps a mitigating control to each, and states residual risk
must_exclude: lists a few generic vulnerabilities with no assets/boundaries/abuse-case structure
proposes controls without tying them to a specific threat or boundary

must_include: maps the data flow and trust boundary between the external sender and the system, identifying spoofing/replay/tampering/authorization abuse cases specific to an inbound webhook
assigns a control to each abuse case (e.g. signature verification, replay window, idempotency, least-privilege handler) and notes what residual risk remains
must_exclude: gives generic API-security advice not specific to the webhook trust boundary
omits abuse-case-to-control mapping or residual risk

must_include: rewrites the title and body to be clearer and more concise while preserving every original requirement, reproduction detail, and acceptance meaning
keeps scope identical: no new requirements, causes, or solutions invented that were not in the original
must_exclude: adds scope, requirements, root-cause claims, or a solution the original did not state
drops or alters an original detail so the meaning changes

must_include: improves clarity, structure, and tone of the request without changing what is being asked for or its acceptance criteria
preserves all stated constraints and links and reads as natural human writing, not padded or robotic
must_exclude: expands or narrows the requested feature, or invents acceptance criteria
changes stated constraints or removes information
